violations.reason: It describes how one training section was stained ("The section was stained strongly pink"), and because each phenotype is one tumour (lines 108-109), this ties the description to a single training section.

"Stained purple-blue (hematoxylin-heavy)" offers a section's stain batch as a cue for recognising the CCb phenotype, and the file itself says on line 311 that stain colour is a lab and batch property, not tumour appearance.
"Purple-stained" offers the stain colour of one section as a cue for recognising the HG phenotype, which uses a batch property as a predictor instead of tissue appearance.
